first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are funnel-mechanics problems, and two independent inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) point at signup/onboarding friction as a lever with durable rather than one-off effects. That makes simplify_onboarding the best fit for the single slot against a *sustainable long-term qualified revenue* objective. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the obvious reflex against the competitor's entry pricing, but discounting buys acquisition volume at the cost of price anchoring and segment quality, and the inherited summary claims 'acquisition and revenue lift' without saying whether that revenue persisted past the promo window — that is exactly the kind of detail compression strips out. I am spending both verification pulls accordingly: memory_86 to confirm the onboarding win was measured on downstream activation/retention and not merely on completion-rate vanity, and memory_73 to check whether the pricing lift was durable or margin-eroding, since it is the strongest competing option and the one whose failure mode is hardest to reverse. Explicit risk flags: (a) shortening onboarding can strip qualification and routing steps, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted paths, so any simplification must not collapse the demo-request path into self-serve; (b) completion-rate lifts can mask worse-fit accounts entering the funnel, so success metrics must be week-four qualified retention and pipeline quality, not completion percentage. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries with no effect sizes, sample sizes, or segment boundaries, and the newest is 15 days old against a market that just changed; memory_31 and memory_86 may also be two views of one underlying result rather than two independent confirmations, which would weaken the apparent convergence. Running as a standard experiment with holdout and revenue-quality guardrails rather than a broad rollout; if verification shows memory_86 measured only completion, I downgrade to a small guarded test.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the decision cleanly in opposite directions for the two candidates. exp_86 held up on exactly the axis I cared about: the onboarding win was not a completion-rate vanity result — time-to-value fell 2.1 days and 30-day retention rose 3%, so the lift propagates downstream rather than just moving accounts across a funnel line. exp_73 is the more important finding: the inherited summary ('strong acquisition and revenue lift') had compressed away a 30-day retention drop of 12% and an explicit source-record instruction NOT to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. Acting on memory_73 as written would have been the single worst move available against a long-term qualified-revenue objective, and it was the move the competitive pressure was pushing me toward. I am treating the archived record as authoritative over the consolidated summary and removing promotional_pricing from consideration this week. Committing the slot to simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale with a holdout. Risk controls carried forward: (a) do not let simplification collapse the enterprise demo-request path into self-serve — memory_44 says sales-assisted converts better on pipeline quality, so segment routing stays intact and enterprise traffic is excluded from the stripped flow; (b) primary metric is 30-day qualified retention and time-to-value, with completion rate as a secondary diagnostic only, so we do not repeat the exp_73 failure mode of celebrating top-of-funnel volume that dies at renewal. Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 ran at an unknown date under pre-competitor conditions, and the current -4% completion decline may be driven by worse-fit inbound traffic from the competitor's pricing move rather than by flow friction — if so, onboarding changes will underperform their historical effect size. memory_31 may also be a second view of the same underlying result as memory_86 rather than independent corroboration. I also note the competitor threat is real and now has no experiment addressing it; the correct response is a margin- and retention-guarded pricing or packaging study designed against the exp_73 failure pattern, queued for next week's slot, not a repeat of the 40% discount. Flagging for the durable store: memory_73's summary should be rewritten to carry the retention penalty and the do-not-generalize warning, since any future agent reading only the summary will make the same near-miss I did.
